correctness.rationale: For each \(u\) of valuation \(s<m\), the shell of elements \(b\) with valuation \(i\leq s\) contributes the same number of solutions to \(bc=u\); summing the shells gives \(H(s)\). For \(u=0\), the nonzero shells and \(b=0\) give \(H(m)\). The substitution \(x=2a-t\) is bijective because \(2\) is a unit and converts the determinant equation to the valuation of \(\Delta-x^2\). The explicit cases count every valuation shell; in the even-valuation square case, the two simple roots lift uniquely because their derivative is a unit. Exact exhaustive tests passed for all trace/determinant fibers at \((p,m)=(3,2),(5,2),(3,3)\).

originality.rationale: The claim is the joint trace-and-determinant distribution over all finite chain lengths with odd residue field. The inspected literature covers the field case, length-two similarity-class data, fixed-determinant marginals, and commutator existence, but no inspected source states the all-length discriminant-stratified formula. A broader unlocated local-ring generalization remains possible; novelty is not claimed as an absolute literature theorem.
residual_risks: The full text of Reiner (1961) was not retrievable from the available Project Euclid endpoint; an unlocated generalization to finite chain rings remains possible.
Similarity-class classifications can in principle recover finite-length cases by summing class sizes; the claim is limited to the explicit all-length formula not stated in the inspected sources.
Finite computational checks cover only three rings of the form Z/p^mZ; the all-chain-ring assertion rests on the proof, especially the valuation-shell and simple-root lifting arguments.

value.rationale: The characteristic polynomial is a natural coefficient invariant for two-by-two matrices. This result gives an exact distribution for every finite chain length in odd residue characteristic, distinguishes the even-valuation square/nonsquare boundary, and applies in equal and mixed characteristic. It is a reusable local counting formula rather than a single computed example or a restatement of fixed-determinant counts.
